messages.subject: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1139738: r-cran-rprojroot: package fails to reproduce due to future timestamp in changelog
messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1139738: r-cran-rprojroot: package fails to reproduce due to future timestamp in changelog
messages.body_plain:
Source: r-cran-rprojroot
Version: 2.1.1-1
Severity: normal
X-Debbugs-Cc: reproducible-bugs at lists.alioth.debian.org, Blair Noctis <ncts at debian.org>
User: reproducible-builds at lists.alioth.debian.org
Usertags: timestamps

Hi Charles,

r-cran-rprojroot current fails to reproduce on
https://reproduce.debian.net [1]. From my analysis this is due to the
timestamp in the debian/changelog being set to the future with respect
to the time of the upload to the Debian archive. This breaks the
automatic clamping of the files in the binary package and makes the
package non reproducible. As the package is arch:all we can't simply
binNMU it. Please upload a new source package with a timestamp not set
to the future. package migrate.

Thanks!

Jochen

[1] https://reproduce.debian.net/all/#r-cran-rprojroot

messages.body_plain:
Le Fri, Jun 12, 2026 at 09:55:05AM +0200, Jochen Sprickerhof a ?crit :
>
>r-cran-rprojroot current fails to reproduce on
>https://reproduce.debian.net [1]. From my analysis this is due to the
>timestamp in the debian/changelog being set to the future with respect
>to the time of the upload to the Debian archive.

Hi Jochen,

I made a new upload of the package, but I do not understand your
explanation:

In the changelog, you can find this timestamp:
https://tracker.debian.org/media/packages/r/r-cran-rprojroot/changelog-2.1.1-1
  -- Charles Plessy <plessy at debian.org>  Thu, 25 Dec 2025 14:47:47 +0900

And in debian-devel-changes there is this one:
https://tracker.debian.org/news/1701212/accepted-r-cran-rprojroot-211-1-source-into-unstable/
Date: Thu, 25 Dec 2025 06:04:22 +0000

This shows that I uploaded the package at 06:04:22 UTC after I
timestamped the changelot at 05:47:47 UTC, isn't it?

In any case please free to (re)open a bug if my upload did not solve the
problem.

Have a nice day,

Charles

messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-team] Bug#1139738: Bug#1139738: r-cran-rprojroot: package fails to reproduce due to future timestamp in changelog
messages.body_plain:
Hi Charles,

* Charles Plessy <plessy at debian.org> [2026-06-13 09:27]:
>I made a new upload of the package, but I do not understand your
>explanation:
>
>In the changelog, you can find this timestamp:
>https://tracker.debian.org/media/packages/r/r-cran-rprojroot/changelog-2.1.1-1
> -- Charles Plessy <plessy at debian.org>  Thu, 25 Dec 2025 14:47:47 +0900
>
>And in debian-devel-changes there is this one:
>https://tracker.debian.org/news/1701212/accepted-r-cran-rprojroot-211-1-source-into-unstable/
>Date: Thu, 25 Dec 2025 06:04:22 +0000
>
>This shows that I uploaded the package at 06:04:22 UTC after I
>timestamped the changelot at 05:47:47 UTC, isn't it?

You are right, sorry and thanks for the upload. 

I just did some more tests and it seems that the package is currently 
not reproducible on reproduce.d.n as that is using ext4, whereas the 
Debian buildds are using tmpfs. It reproduces just fine for me when 
when compiling on thmpfs, even on the reproduce.d.n hosts.

In case you have any idea why, I would be really interested.

Anyway, I hope we will switch reproduce.d.n to tmpfs soon.

Cheers Jochen

messages.body_plain:
Control: reopen -1

Le Sat, Jun 13, 2026 at 09:02:19PM +0200, Jochen Sprickerhof a ?crit :
>
>I just did some more tests and it seems that the package is currently 
>not reproducible on reproduce.d.n as that is using ext4, whereas the 
>Debian buildds are using tmpfs. It reproduces just fine for me when 
>when compiling on thmpfs, even on the reproduce.d.n hosts.

I found it:

$ ? cat debian/rules
#!/usr/bin/make -f

include /usr/share/dh-r/r-cran.mk

%:
	dh $@ --buildsystem R

override_dh_installdocs:
	tar caf tests.tar.xz tests
	dh_installdocs
	rm -rf tests.tar.xz

The owner of the tests.tar.xz files seems to be different in buildds and
in reproducible-builds.  Thanks for catching it up with your
infrastructure.  I will check if this extra complication in the
packaging is really needed.

Cheers,

Charles

* Charles Plessy <plessy at debian.org> [2026-06-14 15:39]:

>

>#!/usr/bin/make -f
>

>

>

>
>The owner of the tests.tar.xz files seems to be different in buildds and
>in reproducible-builds.  Thanks for catching it up with your
>infrastructure.  I will check if this extra complication in the
>packaging is really needed.

Wow thanks, that fixed it :).

Good day,

I would like to take this opportunity to invite you to participate in our short-term and long-term loan funding program.

As a leading global investment and advisory firm, we leverage our expertise to deliver tailored financial solutions, unlock value, and drive sustainable growth. Our capital supports the development of businesses and communities across a diverse range of sectors, including healthcare, sports and leisure, real estate (commercial and residential), renewable energy, construction, oil and gas services, infrastructure, mining, hospitality, shipping, tourism, and technology.

We are continually seeking promising ventures to partner with and support. If this opportunity is of interest to you, we would be pleased to arrange a more detailed discussion at a time that is convenient, whether via email or another preferred communication channel.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to your response and the possibility of working together.

Mohammed K. Faiz
